title: refactor(mcp): remove stdio server
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the local stdio entrypoint, mutable authentication tools, and device-login flow
- Keeps packages/mcp as a private internal core for the hosted stateless Streamable HTTP Worker
- Removes npm publishing, catalog, and npx documentation surfaces
- Preserves current and 2025 stateless HTTP protocol support for managed-agent clients
- Links the archived npm release and final stdio source snapshot

## Verification

- npm test in packages/mcp
- npm test and npm run check in apps/mcp
- node operations/app-management/app.js validate

gist.headline: The hive goes stateless
gist.blurb: The local MCP server has been carefully packed into the archive, leaving a smaller hosted HTTP worker behind. Managed agents keep their stateless protocol path; the old device-login luggage is no longer in the hallway.
gist.summary: Removed the packages/mcp local stdio entrypoint, mutable authentication and device-login tools, npm publishing, and npx/catalog documentation while retaining the hosted stateless Streamable HTTP Worker and both current and 2025 stateless HTTP protocol support.
gist.impact: Managed-agent clients continue using the hosted stateless HTTP MCP service, while the archived npm release and final stdio source snapshot preserve a reference for the retired local-server path.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden shed server room represents the hosted MCP worker: Polli prunes an old stdio cable and device-login key from a thriving HTTP code-plant, while a small CRT robot happily tends the remaining stateless connections. The visual should make the retained HTTP path feel clean, stable, and warmly maintained rather than dramatic.
